Home Research

Outside-in research feeding the Home screen redesign, R2 campaign. Read this before designing in the claude.ai/design session, alongside home-brief.html (which is the inside-out read of what ships today). This document leads with the world — how the field designs Home, the philosophies available, the jobs the screen actually serves — and only then turns to APEX's own decisions. It reports options; it decides nothing.

Provenance and a gap. Five researchers were commissioned. Three delivered: leaders.md (industry teardown), jtbd.md (jobs-to-be-done), evolution.md (adaptive-home architecture). source missing Two did not: rising.md (home-screen philosophies) and baseline.md (the Baseline weight app + integration audit). Sections 2 and 4 are therefore reconstructed by the synthesis lead from the adjacent delivered research and the health-ecosystem specs, and are marked inferred throughout; the Baseline sync reality in §4 is a fresh audit of the repo and D1 schema by the synthesis lead, marked verified. Everything else traces to a named delivered file, shown as source.md at the point of claim.

1How the Field Designs Home

Ten training and health apps torn down top-to-bottom leaders.md. The training-first ones converge on a small set of repeating patterns; the social/content ones (Hevy, Strava) diverge onto a feed and are the cautionary case. The through-line: every leader's brilliance is subtractive; every leader's failure mode is additive.

Repeating patternWho does itWhat it earns
One dominant "today" object Fitbod, Caliber, JuggernautAI, RP, Peloton (via Stack) Answers "what do I do right now?" in under a second, started with one tap. The home's whole job.
Readiness beside the action, never instead of it Whoop dials, Juggernaut readiness score, Fitbod muscle map Frames the day's prescription. Best-in-class modify the prescription (Juggernaut, Fitbod); weaker ones only display it (Whoop, which then lacks rest-day logic).
Progressive disclosure in three tiers Whoop (glance → tap → dig), Strong (per-exercise), Apple (rings → trends) Density without confusion. Whoop's rule: "each tile is a doorway, not a destination." Skip tiering and even correct content reads as confusing (Juggernaut v1).
Program position always visible when a program exists Juggernaut ("how far along"), RP meso-grid, Peloton schedule Periodized training only feels meaningful when today's slot in the larger arc is legible.
Last-time numbers wherever a number is entered Strong, Hevy, Caliber The single highest-leverage logging affordance — pre-fill or display previous weight/reps at the point of entry.
Persistent, reachable start; resumable mid-workout Peloton floating button, Whoop global '+', Strava Record tab State survives navigation and relaunch and surfaces as a resumable banner. (APEX's #70 gap is exactly the missing half of this.)
A few identity metrics on open Juggernaut SBD & Total, Caliber Strength Score, Whoop Recovery % One to three numbers that say "this is who you are right now" — not a wall of stats.
Rest days reframed, never blank Apple (trend averages, "no penalty framing"), Fitbod (rest → recovery on the body map) Rest reads as recovery, not failure. Streak apps (Peloton) handle it worst — a missed day reads as a broken streak.

What only the best have (the differentiators)

  • The app shows its reasoning. Fitbod's recovery map and Whoop's Daily Outlook explain why today looks like this. Prescription + rationale converts algorithm skeptics into trusters. leaders.md
  • A visible autoregulation loop. JuggernautAI and RP close the circle on-screen: readiness / RPE / soreness demonstrably changes tomorrow's numbers. Rare, and precisely APEX's RPE-progression territory.
  • Separation of deciding from doing. Peloton's Stack lets you queue calmly tonight and start with one tap under fatigue tomorrow. No lifting app has stolen this yet.
  • Self vs. social split at the architecture level. Strava's "You" tab concedes that "my training" and "the feed" are different products; leaders never mix consumption content into the action path.
  • A single derived, actionable metric. Caliber's Strength Balance compresses dozens of lift logs into one directive ("your pull lags your push") — the "no vanity metrics" ideal made concrete.
  • Restraint as trust. The most-praised surfaces (Whoop tier 1, Caliber home, Strong's logging screen) show remarkably little.

Failure patterns to avoid

Anti-patternWho fell into itWhat it costs
Social / content feed as the home surfaceHevy, StravaBuries the primary action a tab away; home answers "what did others do?" not "what do I do?"
Recommendation-row merchandisingPeloton picks, Fitness+ upsell rowsTurns a training home into a content catalog; choice overload.
Density without tieringJuggernautAI v1 dashboard, Whoop for novices"Confusing," "tough to read" — right content, wrong disclosure.
Streaks that punish planned restPelotonA designed rest day reads as failure.
Paywall interrupts around the core actionFitbod (double paywall)Friction wrapped around the one thing the user came to do.
Insight without prescriptionWhoop's rest-day gapData that never changes what you do today — informed but directionless.

2Philosophies of a Home Screen inferred

source missing The dedicated philosophies file (rising.md) was not delivered. The taxonomy below is reconstructed by the synthesis lead from the postures observed across leaders.md and the precedents in evolution.md. Treat it as a menu of stances, not a ranking. Each philosophy is a different answer to "what is the home for?"

The Queue / Launcher

Home is a list of things you could start.

Strong's templates, Hevy's routines, Peloton's Stack. Trade: fastest path to starting a known thing, and it separates deciding from doing when you pre-load it — but it holds no opinion about what today should be, and decays into a flat menu of equal choices.

For APEX this would mean a templates/routines list as the landing surface — which jtbd.md names an explicit anti-job ("not a launcher grid of equal choices"). The Stack's deciding-vs-doing idea is worth stealing without adopting the launcher as the whole home.

The Dashboard

Home is a wall of status you read at a glance.

JuggernautAI's dashboard, Whoop pre-2025, Apple's Summary. Trade: everything visible at once, strong for identity metrics — but density without tiering reads as confusing, and it is the likeliest route to vanity metrics.

For APEX this would mean a stats surface — directly against the "not a vanity dashboard" anti-job and the recorded taste that health is a compact bar, never hero. Borrow the identity-metric instinct (a lift or two on open), reject the wall.

The Coach / Synthesis

Home speaks one synthesized directive about today.

Whoop's Daily Outlook, Gentler Streak's "Go Gentler," Fitbod's recovery-justified session. Trade: highest trust when it shows its reasoning and fuses readiness with the plan into one statement — but it demands the app have an opinion and be right; being wrong is loud.

For APEX this would mean recovery × program-state resolved into a single directive line above the start action ("Recovery 33% — today is heavy squats, consider pulling intensity") rather than three raw percentages. This is the posture jtbd.md M3 argues for.

The Ritual

Home is a repeatable daily ceremony with a state machine.

Duolingo's precomputed next step; JuggernautAI's pre-workout readiness check-in as a first-class act. Trade: builds habit and makes "where am I in the loop" legible (pre / mid / post / rest / missed) — but slides into guilt mechanics and streak punishment if unchecked.

For APEX this would mean surfacing the RPE readiness → prescription loop as a pre-workout ritual whose adjusted numbers you immediately see — take the state machine, leave the guilt.

The Feed

Home is a stream of content or social activity.

Hevy, Strava, Google Discover, Spotify. Trade: endless engagement and accountability for its audience — but it optimizes time-on-screen, not shortest-path-to-action, and buries the primary act.

For APEX this would mean the explicit anti-job ("not a feed or notification pile"). APEX's objective function is "shortest path to the right action," the opposite of a feed's. Named here only to be ruled out.

The Adaptive Stack

Home is a ranked stack of state-driven modules over a stable skeleton.

Whoop's post-2025 "stable skeleton, varying content"; Apple's Smart Stacks; the thesis of evolution.md. Trade: evolves without redesign and stays honest if governed hard — but junk-drawers into a feed without a cap and an exit clause, and needs rules (not ML) at n=1.

For APEX this would mean the module-stack architecture explored in §5 — arguably the synthesis of the Coach (a synthesized hero) and the Ritual (state machine) with a governed body beneath it.

3The Jobs Home Must Do

Derived outside-in from how Ben actually uses a periodized strength app across a day, a week, and a cycle jtbd.md. The current layout was treated as a question, not an answer.

Moments of use

Every distinct moment Ben lands on Home, ordered by frequency × stakes. M1 and M2 are mutually exclusive and together own the single hero slot; every other moment must be ignorable when M1/M2 is live.

#MomentWhat Home owes him
M1Walking into the gymThe hero. Today's session named, one large Start target, zero scrolling, ignorable at arm's length.
M2Mid-workout returnThe most stateful moment, today invisible (#70). Resume must be unmissable in one glance: elapsed time, position (3 of 6), one tap to the exact set. Overrides everything. "Start Workout" while a session runs is Home lying.
M3Morning checkToday's plan + recovery stated as a consequence, not a score. One compact line beats three columns of percentages. Health stays secondary.
M4Pre-gym planningSession name, exercise count / rough duration, a route to preview; week-X-of-Y context in one line, not a wall of program UI.
M5Post-workout, same dayA quiet done state: duration, sets, PRs, progression commitments ("↑ next session · 100 lb" is moss, earned). The record must feel written.
M6Rest dayLead with recovery context + what's next + a live door to train anyway (#71). A rest day is a state, not a dead end. Kill the rotating quote or earn it.
M7Off-program / between programsToday homeless (#71). Home must always offer a path to freeform training — quiet on program days, primary in the no-program state. Read "unprogrammed," not "empty."
M8Post-run / pain follow-upMust appear regardless of program state (today a real branch bug), one tap to answer, vanish when resolved. Due-now, not resident.
M9Check-in day (weigh-in / readiness)Due-when-due (#49): appears on the day, one tap, disappears. Same grammar as the pain follow-up — one prompt vocabulary, no bespoke notification species.
M10Program endCelebration is a bounce-through, not a state. The persistent card's job is the next decision — start next / browse — and it must leave gracefully and route to run history (#73).
M11Reflection / planningEntry points, not content: overview ahead (#64), history behind (#63, #73), trends (Progress tab). Home states one line of where-you-are and routes to depth.

Ranked problems a great Home must solve

  1. The in-progress session is invisible (#70). getInProgressSession exists; Home never calls it. The only problem where Home actively misleads. Answer to the brief's "how loud?": the resume surface overrides the hero slot entirely — it is the hero when it exists.
  2. The common case must survive everything else on this list. One glance, one tap, start today. Every added job is a tax on M1 unless hierarchy makes it free. Fixing 3–7 by adding surface area is failing this.
  3. Recovery data is not actionable. Three numbers are a readout, not an instrument. Either it changes a decision (the consequence, one line) or it earns one muted line and no more.
  4. Off-program training is homeless (#71). No-program is a locked door; rest days offer only a quote. A program is the usual shape of training, not a precondition for it.
  5. History is buried (#63, #73). Work done is the product's evidence and has no front door. Home doesn't render history — it gives it an address.
  6. Due-now items have no grammar (#49, pain follow-up). One prompt vocabulary: appears when due, one tap to resolve, vanishes, never stacks.
  7. Program context sprawls. Name + chips + week line + block-colored timeline + calendar rings states the same fact five ways in five-plus hues. State position once, delegate the map to overview (#64).
  8. State transitions are unowned. Completion is a redirect side-effect; dismissal is a flag flipped elsewhere. Each state needs a designed entrance and exit.

Anti-jobs — what Home must NOT become

  • Not a vanity dashboard. No rings, gauges, streaks, tonnage, score-collecting. If a number neither drives an action nor tells a story, it goes.
  • Not a feed or notification pile. Prompts are finite, due-now, self-expiring. No backlog, no badge count, never two prompts competing — Home does triage, not the user.
  • Not a duplicate of the other tabs. Home states one line and routes; it does not re-render the Workout day detail, Progress charts, or a history browser.
  • Not a launcher grid of equal choices. One primary action per state, always; secondary doors are visually subordinate.
  • Not a motivational surface. No rotating quotes, no confetti-at-rest. Moss means earned, and appears only when something was earned.

4Baseline & the Integration Options inferred

source missing The dedicated Baseline file (baseline.md) was not delivered. What follows is the synthesis lead's own audit of the health-ecosystem specs and the live D1 schema, plus the integration spectrum framed as options. The sync finding is verified against the repo; the integration spectrum is a framing for the brainstorm, not a recommendation.

What Baseline is

Baseline is the weight / body-composition app in Ben's modular health ecosystem — a separate, focused iOS app (own repo, own brainstorm) for daily weight and InBody scans with simple trends. It is a deliberate sibling to APEX, kept separate so body-comp tracking doesn't bloat the workout logger. The ecosystem is local-first: each app works offline and pushes to a shared Cloudflare D1 via the health-api Worker. project spec: 2026-03-22-health-ecosystem-design.md

The sync / data reality (verified audit). verified Baseline does not sync to the shared D1 today — because Baseline does not yet exist. The D1 schema already reserves its tables — body_weights and body_comp_scans, with date/updated_at indexes and a UNIQUE date upsert — but the spec notes they are "created now but empty… ready for the weight app when built." No app writes to them. 2026-03-22-health-api-d1-design.md

Meanwhile APEX's own body-weight capture lives in weekly_checkins, which is explicitly excluded from cloud sync (alongside schema_info). So today there is no path by which a weight trend reaches a shared surface at all: Baseline isn't built, its D1 tables are empty, and APEX's check-in weight never leaves the phone. Any "Baseline weight trend on Home" idea is therefore greenfield, not a wiring-up of something already flowing. 2026-03-23-apex-sync-client-design.md

Integration options spectrum — for Ben, no decision

Three levels at which APEX Home could relate to Baseline's weight trend, from loosest to tightest. Presented as a spectrum to choose along, not a recommendation.

OptionWhat it isGainsCosts
Data-level Baseline writes weight/body-comp to the shared D1; APEX reads the trend (pull from D1, or a local cache) and can render it as a module or a line. Apps stay fully separate; only data is shared. Keeps the two apps decoupled (the ecosystem's stated architecture). Home gains a real weight trend with near-zero UI coupling. Reversible — it's one more read source. Exportable to the dashboard too. Requires Baseline to exist and sync first. Adds a cross-app read dependency and a staleness question (what if Baseline hasn't synced today?). Trend is display-only in APEX unless you also let APEX write.
Feature-level APEX embeds a lightweight weigh-in capture itself (the Weigh-In Prompt module already sketched in §5) and writes to the shared body_weights table, while richer body-comp lives in Baseline. Home both reads the trend and logs to it. Home earns the M9 "weigh-in day" job directly — one-tap log without leaving APEX. Fills the trend from day one without waiting on a second app. Uses the reserved D1 table as designed. Blurs the "APEX is the workout logger" boundary Ben drew deliberately. Two apps can now write the same table (dedup / upsert-by-date already handles collisions, but ownership gets fuzzy). Migrates APEX's check-in weight out of the sync-excluded weekly_checkins.
Full merge Baseline is folded into APEX as a body-comp surface/tab; no separate app. Weight, scans, and workouts live in one product and one local DB. One app, one surface, no cross-app sync for weight at all. Simplest data story. Trend is always fresh and local. Directly contradicts the modular-ecosystem decision ("mobile apps are input devices… without bloating APEX"). Grows APEX's scope and Home's job list. Hardest to reverse. The dashboard still needs the D1 copy regardless, so it doesn't remove the sync work — it just relocates it.

Cross-cutting note: whichever option, the dashboard (read-only, web on CF Pages) still wants weight in D1 — so "does the trend reach the cloud?" is a separate axis from "does the trend appear on APEX Home?" A weight-trend module on Home (§5, candidate #12 territory) is compatible with all three options; it only changes where the data comes from.

5The Evolving Home: A Module Stack

Research question: how do you architect a Home that gets better over time instead of being a frozen layout? evolution.md

Make Home a ranked stack of state-driven modules — each a self-contained unit with a trigger, content, one action, and an exit — ordered by deterministic rules over a small context object, governed hard enough that it never becomes a feed.

The layout is frozen (a vertical stack of cards in the locked design language); the contents and order are alive. Shipping an improvement means adding or tuning a module and a rule — never re-architecting the screen. Formally: render( rank( eligible( modules, context ) ) ) over a registry of modules, a context snapshot, a ranking engine (filter → sort by band then score → cap depth), and a dumb renderer with stable identity so reorders animate.

The module contract

A new module ships as one file conforming to the contract plus one registry line — no screen or layout change. Four clauses, two registry obligations:

  • 1 · Trigger. A predicate + score over the pure HomeContext: when am I relevant, how strongly, and until when? Must include an expiry — no module is relevant forever.
  • 2 · Content. A HomeCard descriptor using an existing archetype (hero / statement / prompt / stat). One idea per card. A content that fits no archetype is a design conversation, not a new archetype by default — governance by construction.
  • 3 · Action. At most one primary action. A card with no action must instead tell a story — a state change worth knowing. Action or story; neither is disqualifying.
  • 4 · Exit. Every module names how its instance leaves: state-cleared, auto-expiry, or user-dismissed. Dismissals persist per instance-key and are never overridden.
  • Registry · Band + cap fit. Declare the band; if the band is at its cap, name which module you outrank and why.
  • Registry · Success metric. One sentence: what event counts as this card having earned its slot (its action fired / its story acknowledged), logged automatically.

Twelve candidates over APEX's available context (program position, session state, e1RM logs, Whoop recovery, weigh-ins, running log). Bands: now interrupts · today the day's prescription · signal stories & warnings · ambient everything else.

Ranking sketch: sort by band, then score within band. Caps — now exclusive (suppresses today), today exactly one, signal ≤ 2, ambient ≤ 2; total ≤ 5. Uneventful rest day → [Rest Day], one card, and that's correct. Note the tie to §4: the Weigh-In Prompt (#10) and a body-weight Trend Story are the modules that would consume Baseline data.

Governance against junk-drawer drift

Every card must earn its slot with an action or a story, the stack is capped, and every card must know how it leaves.

Feed-ification — hard depth cap (hero + 3–4), no pagination, no "more for you." A short Home on a quiet day is the system working. Notification pile — the exit clause is mandatory; expiries short; dismissed means gone; prompts capped one per band per day. Junk drawer — the earn-your-slot rule is disqualifying, not advisory; new modules name what they displace; the events log names modules that never fire and they get deleted (cheap — one registry line). Ranker mistrust — deterministic, table-tested; reorders only on state change, animated so causality is visible.

Why rules beat ML at n=1

  • No data. Bandits need thousands of impressions; Ben generates ~5–10 a day. An epsilon-greedy explorer at n=1 just shows the wrong card 10% of the time forever. (BaRT works because Spotify has ~600M users.)
  • The rules are knowable. At n=1 the model of the user is the user — Ben can write his own relevance function. Encoding domain knowledge beats learning it.
  • Trust requires determinism. Same state → same screen. Ben should predict what Home shows before he opens it; surprise should come from his state (a PR, a red recovery), never from a ranker exploring.
  • Debuggability. "Why is this card here?" must have a one-line answer.

Evolution path, each step optional and reversible: rules → logged rules → self-tuning rules → (maybe never) learned ranking. A pinch of adaptivity earns its keep later without ML — dismissal decay (a thrice-dismissed ambient module auto-demotes) and action-rate review over the events log (informing human curation, not runtime reranking).

6Provocations for the Brainstorm

Sharp what-ifs that combine the research above. These are prompts to argue with, not proposals.

  • P1What if Home leads with readiness × program-state as one synthesized directive (the Coach posture) instead of a static Today card plus three recovery numbers — Whoop's Daily Outlook aimed at a lifter?
  • P2What if the wordmark header gives way to state — the top of Home is the day's synthesis, and the "PEX" chrome shrinks into the pinned nav — so the first thing you read is your day, not the brand?
  • P3What if Home is the module stack from §5 end to end, and every existing section (timeline, calendar, health, pain follow-up) has to re-qualify as a module with a trigger, one action, and an exit — or it doesn't ship?
  • P4What if the resume surface (#70) doesn't just win the hero slot — it changes the whole screen's register, the way Duolingo's home escalates as a window closes: a live, urgent, minimal Home while a session is open?
  • P5What if Baseline's weight trend is a module, not a tab (§4 data-level + §5 candidate #12) — Home reads the D1 trend and shows one sparkline line, and Baseline stays a separate capture app?
  • P6Or the inverse: what if the Weigh-In Prompt module makes APEX itself the weight-capture app (§4 feature-level), and "Baseline the separate app" never needs to be built?
  • P7What if the rest-day state leads with recovery and a freeform-train door (#71) instead of a quote — so a rest day is the moment Whoop data is most useful and off-program training finally has a home?
  • P8What if one prompt grammar (appears-when-due, one tap, self-expiring, one-per-band-per-day) absorbs the pain follow-up, weekly check-in (#49), missed-day, and weigh-in — so Home never grows a bespoke notification species again?
  • P9What if Home borrows Caliber's move and shows exactly one derived, actionable metric (a Strength-Balance-style directive) as its identity line — and every other number has to justify itself against it?
  • P10What if the whole "program context" block collapses to one line of position stated once, and the full block/week map, the calendar, and history all become doors (#64, #63, #73) — Home states, the other tabs detail?
  • P11What if we adopt Peloton's deciding-vs-doing split — a calm "queue tomorrow's session" affordance somewhere off-Home — so the gym moment (M1) is pure execution with no decision left in it?
  • P12What if we hold a hard rule that the redesigned Home must be quieter than today while doing strictly more jobs — fewer hues (two), fewer resident sections, more states — and treat any net-additive layout as a failed direction?

None of this is decided. Every table, philosophy, option, and provocation above is input for the claude.ai/design brainstorm — not a layout, not a recommendation, not a constraint. The binding constraints live in home-brief.html §4–5; this document only widens the aperture before that conversation starts.
